<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The detailed evolution of triple star systems is complicated and poorly known. Using archived optical/infrared and gamma-ray data, we identified the pulsar PSR J0435+3233 as a gamma-ray pulsar in a hierarchical triple system, with a helium white dwarf (WD) as a close inner binary companion and a Sun-like star as the distant tertiary. PSR J0435+3233 and the WD companion are in a circular orbit with a period of
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>orb1</jats:sub>
                     = 8.0 days and an eccentricity of
                    <jats:italic>e</jats:italic>
                    = 0.00016. The tertiary is a G-type subgiant with a mass of 0.98(12)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    at a distance of 2.1(4)  kpc from the Earth. By simultaneously fitting the observed spin-period variations of the gamma-ray emission (over 16.7 yr) and radio emission (over 4.9 yr) from PSR J0435+3233, the changes in the inner orbital parameters, the Shapiro delay, Gaia astrometry, and the outer companion mass, we determined the outer elliptical orbit for the tertiary, with a period
                    <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>orb2</jats:sub>
                     = 73.5 yr and an eccentricity
                    <jats:italic>e</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                     = 0.598. The outer orbit is either nearly perpendicular to the inner orbit with a mutual inclination of ∼85
                    <jats:sup>∘</jats:sup>
                    , or moderately inclined by ∼54
                    <jats:sup>∘</jats:sup>
                    . For the former geometry, the pulsar, the WD, and the tertiary star have masses of 1.16(5)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    , 0.273(8)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    , and 0.91(5)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    , respectively; for the latter geometry, the corresponding masses are 1.34(15)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    , 0.305(23)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    , and 1.13(7)
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⊙</jats:sub>
                    . This is a unique triple system for detailed multiband observations and for studying the evolutionary path and dynamic processes of a primordial triple star system. It will ultimately evolve into a system consisting of a neutron star and two WDs.
                  </jats:p>
title: The PSR J0435+3233 Triple System
